On the left, u passes through two cascaded delay elements G_d, giving u[n-1] and u[n-2]; u[n], u[n-1], u[n-2] are scaled by gains g_0, g_1, g_2. On the right, y passes through two cascaded delay elements G_d, giving y[n-1] and y[n-2], scaled by gains g_4 and g_5. A bottom adder sums g_2 u[n-2] and g_5 y[n-2]; a middle adder sums g_1 u[n-1], g_4 y[n-1] and the bottom adder output; a top adder sums g_0 u[n] and the middle adder output. The objective of the following MATLAB code is to estimate the transfer function coefficients a_1, b_0 and b_1 of H(z) = (b_0 + b_1 z^-1) / (1 + a_1 z^-1), given estimated frequency responses H_hat(Omega) for frequencies INCLUDING Omega = 0 and Omega = pi, saved in MATLAB vectors H.mat and Omega.mat, respectively.
1  %% First order transfer function estimation
2
3  % load estimated frequency responses at tested frequencies
4  load('H.mat'); % H is a 1xL matrix with the estimated freq resp
5  load('Omega.mat'); % Omega is a 1xL matrix with the corresponding freq
6
7  % number of frequencies tested
8  L=length(Omega);
9
10 % assert that enough frequencies were tested
11 assert(...); % assert(cond) throws an error if cond is false.
12
13 % matrices for least-squares problem
14 F = zeros(2*L, 3);
15 G = zeros(2*L, 1);
16
17 for l=0:L-1
18     R = abs(H(l+1)); % the magnitude of the estimated freq resp
19     Phi = phase(H(l+1)); % the phase of the estimated freq resp
20     Om = Omega(l+1); % the freq corresponding to the estimated freq resp
21
22     % populate F and G
23     F(2*l+1,:) = ...;
24     F(2*l+2,:) = [-R*sin(Phi-Om), 0, -sin(Om)];
25     G(2*l+1)   = R*cos(Phi);
26     G(2*l+2)   = R*sin(Phi);
27 end
28
29 % now estimate the transfer function coefficients using least-squares
30 Theta = F\G;
31
32 % define the transfer function;
33 % remember, a0 = 1 is not in the Theta parameter vector
34 a = [1; Theta(1)].';
35 b = Theta(2:3).';
